content: I've noticed that various pieces of automation occasionally add or remove the newline at the end of the lean-toolchain file. Is there a definitive answer to whether the lean-toolchain file in a lean project should end with a newline or not? Or is it more complicated than that? To take two random repos on my hard drive -- my current checkout of mathlib4 does have a newline and my current checkout of formal-conjectures does not.
I don't see anything in the docs requiring a new line (my guess is that it's more of a convention for linux text files) :

Not an official answer, but FWIW:

What you call a "newline" is also known as "end of line" (EOL), and is supposed to come at the end of every line, including the last one.
Mathlib also enforces this in CI, and sets the VSCode settings to always add it when you save a file without it.

Both core and mathlib have EOL at the end of their lean-toolchain.
But yeah, it doesn't matter to lake the binary called lake that's actually elan's wrapper
Just FYI, lean-toolchain is not parsed by lake but by elan. Elan simply has binaries that are called lake, lean, etc. which parse the lean-toolchain file and then invoke the proper binary.
I think lake update can cause the newline to be dropped (or at least previously it could)
So is/was this a "bug" in lake? This might explain the phenomena I'm seeing.
